title.en: The Justice Party and Congress movements in Tamil Nadu

text.en: In Madras a new political force appeared in 1916 to speak for non-Brahmins, and in 1920 it formed the government when the Congress boycotted the elections. Meanwhile the Congress was leading hartals and no-tax campaigns.

In 1912 the Madras Dravidian Association was founded, with C. Natesanar as secretary, and in 1916 he set up a hostel for non-Brahmin students.
On 20 November 1916 about thirty non-Brahmins met at Victoria Public Hall in Chennai under P. Thyagarayar, Dr. T.M. Nair and Natesanar, and founded the South Indian Liberal Federation.
The Congress boycotted the 1920 elections, and the Justice Party won 63 of the 98 elected seats.
A. Subburayalu became the first chief minister, and after 1923 the Raja of Panagal led the ministry.
On 18 March 1919 Gandhi addressed a meeting on Marina Beach, and on 6 April a hartal protested the Rowlatt Act with prayer and fasting.
Rajaji, Kasturirangar, S. Satyamurty and George Joseph addressed the Marina meeting.
Khilafat Day was observed on 17 April 1920 under Maulana Shaukat Ali, and Vaniyambadi was the centre of the Khilafat agitation.
Rajaji and E.V. Ramaswamy, later Periyar, led the Non-Cooperation Movement in Tamil Nadu, working with Yakub Hasan.
There was a no-tax campaign in Thanjavur, a temperance movement against liquor, and a boycott of councils, schools and courts.
The visit of the Prince of Wales on 13 January 1922 was boycotted.
The Swarajists did not accept office, so P. Subbarayan, an independent, formed a ministry, and the Justice Party stayed in office until 1937.
S. Satyamurti headed the Simon Boycott Propaganda Committee, and black flags greeted the Commission at Madras on 18 February 1929.
In 1927 a campaign demanded removal of the statue of James Neill, who was brutal after the Cawnpur massacre.

problem.en: How did the Justice Party come to power in 1920?

text.en: The Congress boycotted the 1920 elections under the Act of 1919.
The Justice Party won 63 of 98 elected seats in the Council.
It remained in office, with a break, till 1937.

why.en: The Raja of Panagal led after 1923.
